items.abstract: <jats:title>summary</jats:title><jats:p>Exact expressions for the distribution function of a random variable of the form c<jats:sub>1</jats:sub>χ<jats:sup>2</jats:sup><jats:sub>m</jats:sub>+c<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>χ<jats:sup>2</jats:sup><jats:sub>n</jats:sub> are given where χ<jats:sup>2</jats:sup><jats:sub>m</jats:sub> and χ<jats:sub>2</jats:sub><jats:sub>n</jats:sub>χ<jats:sup>2</jats:sup><jats:sub>n</jats:sub> are independent chi‐square random variables with m and n degrees of freedom respectively. (The positive c<jats:sub>i</jats:sub> are distinct). In particular, the exact asymptotic distribution function for the average Kendall tau statistic is written as a function of tables of Solomon (1960) and some found in Abramowitz and Stegun's <jats:italic>Handbook of Mathematical Functions.</jats:italic></jats:p>
